title: $f^!$ preserves integral constructible complexes
statement:
For every separated morphism of finite type $f:X\to Y$, the right adjoint
$f^!$ of [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] maps $\Dctf(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into
$\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Its restriction is right adjoint to
$Rf_!:\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)\to\Dctf(Y,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Work in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: the schemes are separated and of finite type over the standing field, with $\ell$ invertible. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, one of the allowed coefficient rings of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The coefficients are the condensed valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and its pulled-back module-object sheaves, as in the statement's categories, not discrete constant $\mathcal O_E$-sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], the standing schemes are qcqs: their structure maps to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are separated and of finite type. For these schemes, clause (2) of [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] gives $\Dctf(T,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ and equality of their localizing closures. We may therefore prove the assertion using $\Dbc$ throughout. Fix $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$.

source.place: clause (2), specialized to the integral coefficient ring

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $V_\beta=\operatorname{Spec}A_\beta$ of the quasi-compact scheme $Y$. By the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each $f^{-1}(V_\beta)$ has a finite cover by affine opens $U_{\beta\alpha}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{\beta\alpha}$ with $B_{\beta\alpha}$ finitely generated over $A_\beta$. Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$; evaluation $A_\beta[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\twoheadrightarrow B_{\beta\alpha}$ identifies $B_{\beta\alpha}$ with its source modulo the kernel. The affine-quotient characterization of [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives a closed immersion $i:U_{\beta\alpha}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_{V_\beta}$. With projection $p$ and open inclusions $u:U_{\beta\alpha}\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V_\beta\hookrightarrow Y$, we have $fu=vpi$. These finitely many opens $U_{\beta\alpha}$ cover $X$.

source.place: Existence of charts; the finitely generated algebra presentation is written out

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$ for each scheme in a chart. The integral functors $Rh_!$ and their right adjoints on these categories are those of [det-prop-int-brown-construction] and [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. The chart schemes $U$, $V$ and $\mathbf A^d_V$ are affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-separated, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes the inclusions $u$ and $v$ quasi-compact. Clause (1) of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] therefore supplies $u_!\dashv u^*$ and $v_!\dashv v^*$ here. The compact-support composition comparison and $fu=vpi$ give $Rf_!u_!\simeq v_!Rp_!Ri_!$. Thus, for every $A\in\mathcal T_U$, the natural bijections are
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A,u^*f^!K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(u_!A,f^!K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!u_!A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rp_!Ri_!A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!Ri_!A,v^*K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,i^!p^!v^*K).$$
This yields $u^*f^!K\simeq i^!p^!v^*K$. Explicitly, a natural bijection between these two represented Hom functors sends the identity of the first representing object to a map from it to the second, and the inverse bijection sends the second identity to the reverse map; naturality makes both composites identities. These are adjunctions on the localizing categories, so no constructibility of $f^!K$ is assumed in this calculation.

The integral projective-line and affine-space theorem [det-thm-int-restriction-line] supplies $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$, $q^!\simeq q^*(1)[2]$, $p^!\simeq p^*(d)[2d]$, and preservation of $\Dbc$ by these shifted twisted pullbacks. For the chart above, $v^*K\in\Dbc(V,\mathcal O_E)$ by [sk-lem-int-tensor], and hence $p^!v^*K\in\Dbc(\mathbf A^d_V,\mathcal O_E)$. The integral closed-immersion theorem [det-thm-int-restriction-closed] then gives $i^!p^!v^*K\simeq R\underline\Gamma_U(p^!v^*K)\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$. Applying the preceding isomorphism shows $u^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$ on every member of the finite cover.

source.place: Projective line and affine space; Closed immersions; General f, first sentence

proof.text:
Apply only clause (1) of [det-thm-int-restriction-glue] to $M=f^!K$ and the finite open cover just constructed: it gives $f^!K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Also $Rf_!$ preserves $\Dbc$ by [det-prop-int-brown-construction]. For $A\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ the adjunction of [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)}(Rf_!A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)}(A,f^!K).$$
Indeed these full-subcategory Hom sets are exactly the ambient Hom sets. Naturality in $A$ and $K$ is inherited from the ambient adjunction, so the restricted functors are adjoint. Translating by the equalities in step 1 proves both assertions for $\Dctf$. This does not invoke clause (2) of the gluing node, which already restates the item.
